title: Lift short multiples through bounded prefix spans

add.statement: For any rank-$d$ lattice $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb Z^I$ with basis matrix $B$ and the uniform box sampler on $\{2,\ldots,g+1\}^I$, its largest fiber density is at most $g^{-d}$. For every stack $\mathbf W$ with either sampler, $\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)\le g^{-\operatorname{rank}\mathbf W}$, and $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top)\ge\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)$ for each vector $v$ in its row space. In the lattice case let $A=B^\top$. In the stack case let $A$ be the vertical concatenation of the $W_c$, omitting column $0$ if it is zero. In each case the retained tuple consists of the sampled coordinates indexed by the columns of $A$, with original indices.
add.proof:
In the centered sampler the formula for $r_0$ translates $r_\star$, so given all positive-index draws it is uniform on $g$ consecutive integers.
Reduction modulo $q$ is injective on each such interval since $g<q$.
Extend the nonzero column $0$ to a column basis when retained in the stack case, and otherwise choose any column basis of $A$.
Given the coordinates outside that basis, a fiber requires a unique tuple of basis coordinates if it is attainable, by column independence.
The chain rule bounds the required tuple probability by $g^{-\operatorname{rank}A}$, with atom $1/g$ per independent box coordinate and conditional atom at most $1/g$ for the centered coordinate when present.
Averaging the conditional bound gives the asserted fiber-density bound.
The linear image $v^\top r$ of the stack output has maximum atom at least as large, since its atom over a maximizing stack output contains that event.

add.statement: Every nonzero usable stack of rank at most three whose row space contains no kernel vector has a witness of $S$ in its row space.
add.proof:
Work over $K=\mathbb F_{q^n}$, with $a=n/2-1$, $b=n/2$, $c=n/2+1$ and $I=\{a,b,c\}$.
Set $(Z_a,Z_b,Z_c)=(W_U,W_V,\sigma^c(W_U))$.
Writing $z_s=\sigma^s(z)$, the three defining tie polynomials reduce modulo $P$ to $Z_s z_t-Z_t z_s$ for the pairs $(a,b),(a,c),(b,c)$ by the substitution action of $\sigma$.
Thus $Z_s z_t=Z_t z_s$ for all three pairs.
Choose a basis matrix $B$ for the row space $\mathcal V$ of dimension $d$, and write its rows as $u_i^\top$.
As linear combinations of symmetric stack matrices, the $Z_s$ have both row and column spaces in the extension of $\mathcal V$.
Take a base-field left inverse $C$ of $B$ and set $M_s=C Z_s C^\top$.
Then $B M_s B^\top=Z_s$ because the projection $BC$ fixes the row and column spaces of $Z_s$.
At least one of $M_a,M_b$ is nonzero since recovering $Z_a,Z_b$ by this factorization recovers all stack coefficients.
Let $h_s=B^\top z_s$ for all $s$.
Since $B$ has base-field entries, $h_s=\sigma^s(h_0)$.
The entries of $h_0$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb F_q$ since a relation on them gives a vector of $\mathcal V$ in the kernel of $z$.
The entries of $h_a$ remain independent over $\mathbb F_q$ since $\sigma^a$ is an automorphism fixing the base field.
The Moore determinant demand makes the first $d$ of $h_a,h_b,h_c$ a basis, as its matrix has the successive Frobenius powers of the entries of $h_a$ as its rows.
By injectivity of $B$, the reduced ties give $M_s h_t=M_t h_s$.
For any scalars $\lambda_s$ indexed by $I$, summing the ties gives $(\sum_s\lambda_s M_s) h_t=M_t(\sum_s\lambda_s h_s)$ for each $t$.
Since the $h_t$ span, that equality gives $\ker(\lambda\mapsto\sum_s\lambda_s h_s)\subseteq\ker(\lambda\mapsto\sum_s\lambda_s M_s)$.
Consequently $h_s\mapsto M_s$ defines a linear map $M$.
The trilinear form $L(x,y,z')=y^\top M(x)z'$ is symmetric in its last two arguments by symmetry of the matrices.
Extending the reduced ties by bilinearity gives $M(x)z^{\prime}=M(z^{\prime})x$ for all $x,z^{\prime}$.
For each $i>0$ the Booleanity test yields $L(h_s,u_i,u_i-u_0)=0$ since it holds on the linear combination of stack matrices $Z_s$.
By spanning, $L(x,u_i,u_i-u_0)=0$ for every $x$.
Also $Z_a=\sigma^a(Z_c)$ by $a+c=n$.
Since $Z_b=W_V$ only has even powers of $T$, $\sigma^b(Z_b)=Z_b$ by $\omega^b=-1$.
Applying $Z\mapsto C Z C^\top$ over the base field gives $M_s=\sigma^s(M_{n-s})$ for $s=a,b$.
Suppose first that $u_0=0$ and choose a basis $(l_1,\ldots,l_d)$ from the rows $u_i$.
The Booleanity identities give $L(x,l_i,l_i)=0$ for all $x$ in this case.
By symmetry, all tensor coordinates with a repeated index vanish.
If $d<3$ there are no other coordinates, so $L=0$.
For $d=3$ the off-diagonal entries of $M_s$ on basis pairs are $t=L(l_1,l_2,l_3)$ times the coordinate of $h_s$ in the complementary slot, by symmetry.
Comparing those coordinates in $M_s=\sigma^s(M_{n-s})$ gives $t h_s=\sigma^s(t)h_0$ for $s=a,b$.
Independence of $h_a,h_b$ in dimension three forces $t=0$ by these equations.
So $L=0$ also in dimension three.
The zero form is impossible since at least one of $M_a,M_b$ is nonzero, so $u_0\ne0$.
Extend $l_0=u_0$ to a basis using rows $l_i=u_{j_i}$ for $1\le i<d$.
For $\delta\in\{0,1\}^{d-1}$ define $p_\delta$ by $l_0^\top p_\delta=1$ and $l_i^\top p_\delta=\delta_i$, and set $w_\delta=B p_\delta$.
For $i>0$ the Booleanity identities give $L(x,l_i,l_i)=L(x,l_i,l_0)$.
By symmetry and these reductions, each tensor coordinate depends only on the set of positive indices it contains.
On the Boolean cube the squarefree monomials are a basis of functions by triangularity under subset inclusion.
The form $(x,y,z^{\prime})\mapsto(x^\top p_\delta)(y^\top p_\delta)(z^{\prime}^\top p_\delta)$ has coordinate $\prod_{i\in A}\delta_i$ at a basis triple with positive index set $A$.
Thus these forms span the tensors with the stated coordinates by invertibility of the evaluation matrix.
Write $M(x)=\sum_\delta C_\delta (x^\top p_\delta)p_\delta p_\delta^\top$ using this expansion.
The matrices $p_\delta p_\delta^\top$ are independent since their evaluations on pairs of basis rows give all the same squarefree monomials for $d-1\le 2$.
For $z_\delta=h_0^\top p_\delta$, independence of the entries of $h_0$ gives $z_\delta\ne0$ because $p_\delta$ is a base-field vector with $l_0^\top p_\delta=1$.
Comparing coefficients in $M_s=\sigma^s(M_{n-s})$ now gives $C_\delta\sigma^s(z_\delta)=\sigma^s(C_\delta) z_\delta$ for $s=a,b$.
Dividing the coefficient equations gives $x_\delta=\sigma^a(x_\delta)=\sigma^b(x_\delta)$ for $x_\delta=C_\delta/z_\delta$.
Applying $\sigma^{-a}$ to $\sigma^a(x_\delta)=\sigma^b(x_\delta)$ gives $x_\delta=\sigma(x_\delta)$.
Write $\chi_\delta=C_\delta/z_\delta\in\mathbb F_q$ by the fixed field of Frobenius.
Any linear test $\varrho$ with base-field coefficients vanishes on $Z_a,Z_b,Z_c$ because it vanishes on every stack entry.
The resulting equations are $h_0^\top A_\varrho h_s=0$ for $s=a,b,c$, with $A_\varrho=\sum_\delta\chi_\delta\varrho(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)p_\delta p_\delta^\top$ by the expansion.
Spanning gives $h_0^\top A_\varrho=0$.
The base-field entries of $A_\varrho$ and independence of the entries of $h_0$ give $A_\varrho=0$.
Independence of the squares gives $\chi_\delta\varrho(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)=0$ for every $\delta$.
Some $\chi_\delta$ is nonzero since otherwise the expansion gives $M=0$.
For that $\delta$, dividing the test equations by $\chi_\delta$ gives $\varrho(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)=0$ for every test.
The Booleanity tests force $(w_\delta)_i\in\{0,1\}$ since they give $(w_\delta)_i^2=(w_\delta)_i$.
The constraint tests certify that this Boolean assignment in $\mathcal V$ is a witness because each term $a^\top(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)b$ evaluates to the corresponding product $(a^\top w_\delta)(b^\top w_\delta)$.

add.statement: The difference $G_T-\mathsf K^\alpha$ of the two received target-group expressions has zero stacks in both sectors.
add.proof: Every stack entry of this difference is zero by definition, since its only nonzero pairing coefficient is indexed by $(G_1,G_2)$ rather than a left-factor and right-factor pair.

add.statement: Let $v\in\mathbb F_q^{N+1}$ be a nonzero kernel vector with $v_0=0$ and $x\in\mathbb Z^{N+1}$ a short multiple, so $x\equiv c v\pmod q$ for a nonzero $c\in\mathbb F_q$ and $\|x\|_\infty\le\beta$. Let $A$ be columns $1,\ldots,\ell$ of $M$. Form $\hat x\in R^\ell$ by the coefficient packing of the forms with integer entries. Then $A\hat x=0\pmod q$ and $0<\|\hat x\|_\infty\le\beta$.
add.proof:
With $v_0=0$, the defining coefficient blocks of $z(v)=0$ are those of $A\hat v$, where $\hat v$ is the packing over $R_q$.
By linearity of $x\mapsto A\hat x\bmod q$, $A\hat x\equiv c A\hat v=0\pmod q$.
The coefficients of $\hat x$ are positive-index entries of $x$ or padding zeros, so the sup norm is at most $\beta$.
At least one of these coefficients is nonzero modulo $q$ because $cv\ne0$ has zeroth coordinate zero.

add.statement: Fix admissible points and a symmetric matrix $W$. For $\chi\in\mathbb F_q$ and $e\in\{0,1\}$ let $N_e=P_W-Z_0R_W-e\chi L_\rho$ and $Z_e=Z(X)(X-\rho)^e$, and let $\gamma$ generate the order-$\nu$ subgroup $\mathcal G$ used for the cosets. The identity $P_W=h'Z+Z_0 R$ with $\deg h'<D$ and allowed $R$ holds for some such $h',R$ exactly if $W$ passes. The identity $P_W-\chi L_\rho=h Z(X)(X-\rho)+Z_0 R$ with $\deg h<D-1$ and allowed $R$ holds for some such $h,R$ exactly if $W$ passes and $\chi=W_{00}$. In each identity $R$ must equal $R_W$. A moment matrix $ww^\top$ of a witness passes, so it satisfies both identities with the prescribed corner.
add.proof:
Evaluation of either division identity on the cosets gives $R(p)=P_W(p)/Z_0(p)$ there.
Interpolation in degree below $
u n_{\mathsf c}$ forces $R=R_W$.
On the roots of $Z_e$ ordered by $d_j$, cosets, then the optional $ho$, the table gives the evaluation vector of $N_e$ as $((P_W(d_j))_j,0,(W_{00}-\chi)_{i=1}^e)$.
By the factor theorem these values give exactly the divisibility conditions for the two identities.
The residual degrees at most $2D-2$ and divisor degrees $D-1,D$ give quotient degrees below $D,D-1$, respectively.
Geometric summation in $\sum_j a_j\delta^j\sum_{i=0}^{
u-1}(\gamma^j)^i$ gives the coset sum of $R_W=\sum_j a_j X^j$ as $

The arguments $\delta^
u$ are distinct over the distinct cosets because the kernel of the $

By the root bound and $

u m}$ vanish, vacuously if there are no cosets.
The test table identifies passing with the vanishing of the values $P_W(d_j)$ and the coset sums of $R_W$.

add.statement:
Fix the admissible parameters and matrix $M$ of the extraction experiment. Let $\mathsf{D}$ be an expression of $\mathbb{G}_T$, $\chi \in \mathbb{F}_q$, and $r, r' \in \mathbb{F}_q^{N+1}$.

 
(a) \emph{Passing stacks.} If $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$, then in each sector $\mathsf{s}$ the stack $\mathbf{W}^{\mathsf{s}}(\mathsf{D})$ passes and satisfies the ties, $W^{\mathsf{s}}_c(\mathsf{D})\, r = u^{\mathsf{s}}_c(\mathsf{D})$ for every cell $c$, and the corner $\bigl( W^{\mathrm{plain}}_{c_{\mathrm{key}}}(\mathsf{D}) \bigr)_{00}$ is $\chi$.
(b) \emph{Locus.} If $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$ and $W^{\mathsf{s}}_c(\mathsf{D})\, r' = u^{\mathsf{s}}_c(\mathsf{D})$ for every sector and cell, then $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r'$. In particular, if $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$ and has zero stacks, then $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ formally, and $\chi = 0$.
(c) \emph{Coincidence.} If $\mathsf{D}$ is not $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$, $\Pr[\operatorname{val}(\mathsf{D}; \mathbf{c}, r) = \chi\kappa] \le d_f/(q - D) \le \varepsilon_f$ for uniform valid $\mathbf{c}$.
(d) \emph{No formal key scalar.} If $\chi \ne 0$, then $\mathsf{D}$ is not $\chi\kappa$ formally.
(e) \emph{Source groups.} If $\mathsf{E}$ and $\mathsf{E}'$ are expressions of $\mathbb{G}_1$, or of $\mathbb{G}_2$, that are not formally equal, then for every $r$ their values at $(\mathbf{c}, r)$ are equal with probability at most $\varepsilon_f$ over $\mathbf{c}$. If $\mathsf D$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at fixed $r$, the coefficient on each pair with second-group leaf $H_{j,1}^{\mathrm{leg}}$ in its sector is zero unless its first-group index is $F_{i,1}^{k_1}$, in which case it equals the corresponding coefficient on $F_{i,2}^{k_1},H_{j,2}^{\mathrm{leg}}$. The kind $\mathrm X$ and exponent in $s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_c}y_i$ identify cell $c$ and row $i$. Formally equal target-group expressions have equal stacks. For the proof use $U=2^{\lambda+1}$, $d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6$, and $\varpi=\Omega_{22}\zeta\zeta^{\prime}\zeta^{\prime\prime}\varepsilon$. Factor symbols with final index 1 or 2 denote the published coordinates for the indicated left index or right leg, $h^1_j$ denotes the first entry of $H^{\mathrm{leg}}_j$ for that leg, and $W_c,u_c$ denote the stack and vector of the sector currently considered.
add.proof:
Condition (P2) and $2^{\ell_{\mathsf{lab}}}\ge q$ give $N_{\mathsf{free}}>0$.
From its other nonnegative terms at $U>0$ and $L\ge1$, $E(U)\ge (8U+8)\varepsilon_f$.
By adding the inequalities in (P5), $E(U)\le1$.
The bound $(8U+8)\varepsilon_f\le1$ gives $d_f<q-D$ by $\varepsilon_f=(d_f+61)/(q-D)$.
Each valid-coin coordinate excludes at most $\max(D,K_1+1)=D$ values since $K_1\le n/2$ and $n\le D$.
For fixed $r$, multiplying $\operatorname{val}(\mathsf D)-\chi\kappa$ by $\varpi$ gives a polynomial of degree at most $d_f$ by the degree demand.
The valid coin samples form an independent product by their sampling rules.
The factor $\varpi$ is nonzero on their support because its five factors are sampled nonzero.
Schwartz–Zippel bounds the coincidence probability for a nonzero polynomial by $d_f/(q-D)\le\varepsilon_f$.
Since that bound is less than one, identity on the valid grid is equivalent to the cleared polynomial being zero.
For an identity divide by $\varpi$ in the Laurent ring in its factors, where $y$ and $\tau$ are still polynomial variables.
Let $a$ denote a first-group leaf, with exponent $\tilde a$ when $\Omega_{22}=0$.
Write $\beta_{a,j,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}$ for the coefficient with $H_{j,1}$ minus the $F_{i,2},H_{j,2}$ coefficient in the same cell and sector when $a=F_{i,1}$.
From the hidden-basis formulas, the coefficient of $\Omega_{22}^{-1}$ at positive $\Omega_{12}$ powers is $-\Omega_{12}\sum_{a,j,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}\beta_{a,j,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}\tilde a\alpha_{\mathsf s}s_{\mathrm{leg}}(B_j(\tau)-y_j)$.
The right side of the identity is independent of the hidden basis, so that sum is zero.
Substitute $y=B(\tau)+t e_j$ and take coefficient $t$ to obtain $\sum_{a,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}\beta_{a,j,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}\tilde a|_{y=B(\tau)}\alpha_{\mathsf s}s_{\mathrm{leg}}=0$.
The left-leaf factors here are $1,\zeta\tau^k,\zeta'\tau^k,\zeta''B_i(\tau),\pi_{k_1}B_i(\tau),\Omega_{12}\pi_{k_1}B_i(\tau)$ by their exponent formulas.
The polynomials $B_i$ are independent because their evaluations at the $d_j$ give the identity matrix.
The kind and exponent recover $k_2,k_1$ by quotient and remainder of half the exponent rounded down modulo $K_1$, with $k_1=0$ for a leg.
At $\varepsilon^0$ the product $\pi_{k_1}s_{\mathrm{leg}}$ is $\pi s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_c}$ by the scalar formulas.
Taking that coefficient in the sum leaves distinct monomials in the sector, scalars, and $\upsilon$, except for the indexed families $B_i$ or distinct powers of $\tau$.
Hence independence of these families in their respective monomials gives $\beta_{a,j,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}=0$ for all indices.
Take the component of $\pi$-degree one, zero degrees in $\zeta,\zeta',\zeta''$, and total hidden-basis degree zero, separately for each power of $\alpha$.
The paired coefficient in the selected sector equals $\chi_{\mathsf s}\kappa$ after moving the key leaf to the right, with $\chi_{\mathrm{plain}}=\chi$ and $\chi_\alpha=-\mathsf D_K$.
From the leaf formulas these pairs are matched $F,H$ terms, $F_{i,1}$ with search bases or $G_2$, quotient and remainder powers with corresponding bases, and $Y_i$ with cancellation bases.
Matched pairs give $F_i^{k_1}H_j^{\mathrm{leg}}$ because $\Omega\Omega^{-1}=1$.
Multiplication of these two coordinates gives $F_i^{k_1}H_j^{\mathrm{leg}}=\gamma_c(y_i r_j+y_iA_j-A_i y_j+A_iB_j)+\pi_{k_1}y_i\vartheta_{\mathrm{leg},j}$, with $A_i,B_i$ evaluated at $\tau$.
The quotient contributions in the selected sector are $\gamma_c Z_c(\tau)h_c(\tau)$ by cancellation of $\zeta$, where $h_c(X)=\sum_{k,j}\mathsf D_{\mathsf P_k^{\mathrm{quo}},(\mathsf B_{c,j}^{\mathrm{quo}})^{\mathsf s}}X^{k+j\Delta}$ over the published pairs.
The remainder contributions in the selected sector are $\gamma_c Z_0(\tau)R_c(\tau)$ by cancellation of $\zeta'$, where $R_c(X)=\sum_{k,j}\mathsf D_{\mathsf P_k^{\mathrm{rem}},(\mathsf B_{c,j}^{\mathrm{rem}})^{\mathsf s}}X^{k+j\Delta'}$ over the published pairs.
The ranges of $k,j$ and $\nu\mid\Delta'$ give only allowed exponents $k+j\Delta'<J'\Delta'=\nu n_{\mathsf c}$ in $R_c$.
Collecting the terms containing $s_{\mathrm X}$ gives $\sum_c\gamma_c b_c$ with $b_c=y^\top(W_c r-u_c)+y^\top(W_c-W_c^\top)A(\tau)+(P_{W_c}+h_c Z_c+Z_0R_c)(\tau)$.
The other terms contain no $s_{\mathrm X}$ because tie masks, cancellation bases and the generator lack these factors.
The coefficient of $\pi s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_c}\varepsilon^0$ gives $b_c=\chi_{\mathsf s}L_\rho$ at the key cell and zero at every other cell.
Consequently the sum of the remaining terms is zero.
At $\tau=d_0$ the coefficient of $y$ in each $b_c$ identity gives $W_c r=u_c$ because $A(d_0)=0$.
The same coefficient at $\rho,d_1,\ldots,d_N$ makes $W_c-W_c^\top$ annihilate $e_0,e_1-e_0,\ldots,e_N-e_0$.
These vectors span, so each $W_c$ is symmetric.
The constant-in-$y$ quotient identities force the proper quotient degrees by comparing their numerators of degree at most $2D-2$ with $\deg Z_c$.
The QAP demand gives passing for every cell from those identities and identifies the key corner as $\chi_{\mathsf s}$.
The coefficient of $\varepsilon^0$ in each even or odd leg mask product $\pi_{k_1}\vartheta_{\mathrm{leg}}$ is $\pi[\upsilon^{k_c}(\eta_1z_\circ+\eta_2z_+)-(-\omega\upsilon)^{k_c}(\eta_2z_-+\eta_3z_\circ)]$ by multiplication of the mask factors.
For a V leg the same coefficient is $\pi\upsilon^{k_c}(\eta_3z_+-\eta_1z_-)$.
Summing these contributions against $y^\top W_c$ gives $\pi\sum_a\eta_a y^\top t_a(\upsilon)$ by the defining three tie polynomials.
The other terms of $\eta_a\varepsilon^0$ are from the tie bases and have factor $P(\upsilon)$.
Taking the $\pi\eta_a\varepsilon^0 y_i$ coefficient of the remaining zero identity gives $(t_a)_i=0\pmod P$ for every $a,i$.
Substituting $h^1_j=s_{\mathrm{leg}}(r_j+A_j)+\vartheta_{\mathrm{leg},j}$ into the supported exponent pairs gives change $\sum_{\mathsf s}\alpha_{\mathsf s}\sum_c\gamma_c y^\top W_c(r'-r)$.
This difference vanishes if the equations $W_c r'=u_c$ hold in both sectors, establishing the locus claim.
If both stacks vanish, that difference is zero for every $r'$, giving a formal identity.
For a formal identity the equations $W_c r'=u_c$ for arbitrary $r'$ force $W_c=0$.
Its plain key corner is therefore zero, forcing $\chi=0$.
Applying this result to the difference of formally equal expressions shows their stacks agree.
For two source-group expressions, pair their difference with the opposite generator to obtain a target expression having zero stacks by its pairing coordinates.
A formally distinct pair makes this target difference nonformal by nondegeneracy.
Since a zero-stack identity at any $r$ would be formal, use the target coincidence bound for this difference at every $r$.

add.statement: Under the extraction theorem's hypotheses, if the adversary runs in time $t$ with at most $Q$ generic group calls and $Q_H$ queries to each random oracle, both $\mathcal B_0,\mathcal B_1$ run within $t_R=t+O(Q+d_R Q_H+\mu)+\mathsf{poly}(D,\log q)$ in the specified operations model including description and advice. Use $\ell_{\mathsf{lab}}$ for the label bit length and $Q_H$ for the per-oracle cap.
add.proof:
Independence in (R2) allows the private and recovery points to be drawn before the run.
The identities $(k+1)d_R=n$ and $\ell=\lceil N/d_R\rceil$ give $(k+1)(\ell+1)d_R\le D(D+2)$ using $N,n\le D$.
Counting the leaf indices gives $O((K_1+K_2+1)(N+1)+n(J+J'+1)+\Delta+\Delta')$ received leaves.
This is polynomial in $D$ by $K_1K_2=n/2$, $J\Delta\le2D$ and $J'\max(1,\Delta')\le D$.
The fixed QAP coefficient lists occupy $O(ND+D)$ advice by their degrees.
The private, recovery and encryption coordinates are sampled in polynomial time by the independent finite-set draws in (R2) and encryption, apart from its centered search coordinate.
The excluded sets for the coin draws have polynomial-size descriptions by their explicit point and left-leg lists.
The centered sampler costs $O(N+1)$ draws and integer operations on values bounded by $B<q\le2^{\ell_{\mathsf{lab}}}$ by its explicit formula.
The seeded challenge programming takes polynomial time by the bound on its ring coefficient count.
Evaluating the form definition on coordinate vectors by ordinary ring convolution constructs the $n(N+1)$ coefficients in polynomial time by the ring-size bound.
Horner evaluation of the listed polynomials and scalar-factor arithmetic then give polynomial-size leaf exponent circuits.
The masked message takes $O(\mu)$ additional description and operations by packing it into label-sized blocks for writes and XORs.
Keep the partial injection in both directions in tables and record strings known to be outside its image.
Conditional on the tables the unused injection is uniform into the undecided strings, by symmetry of a uniform injection.
A new exponent gets a uniform undecided string by the allowed exclusion sample.
A previously undecided string is valid with probability $A/U$ for $A$ unused exponents and $U$ undecided strings by uniformity of the remaining injection.
A uniform draw in $[0,U-1]$ compared to $A$ implements this decision, with $U<2^{\ell_{\mathsf{lab}}}$ once generators' labels are allocated.
Conditional on validity its exponent is uniform among unassigned ones by symmetry.
A name query uses the eligibility flag and opposite exponent lookup-or-assign rule in constant time, using a fresh undecided string when necessary.
Each generic group call thus takes constant extra time by the tables and at most two operand exposures and one result.
Initial label assignments cost polynomial time by applying the new-exponent rule to the leaves and the key.
For a fresh seed query the allowed ring sample takes $d_R$ field samples.
For a fresh key query the answer is one sample in the oracle's finite range by the sampling operation.
Each oracle query adds constant table work, so the total oracle overhead is $O(d_R Q_H)$.
Use scalar arithmetic circuit pointers for the records, with a zero pointer for an operand without a record as prescribed.
The linear and pairing rules add $O(1)$ gates per result.
Keeping the private-point value of each new gate makes the comparison in (R3) constant time per result.
Saving the two pointers at the first discrepancy makes its difference one extra subtraction gate.
The target record in (R3) is a table lookup.
Zeroing the other sector's right-group and key leaves projects precisely to the desired sector by the target expression formula, with generators assigned to the plain sector.
The denominators of the leaf formulas are fixed nonzero coin values at a recovery point, so the resulting $r$-circuit uses only polynomial gates.
The resulting circuit in $r$ has $O(Q)+\mathsf{poly}(D,\log q)$ gates by the per-call and leaf-size bounds.
The gradient-cost demand gives the same asymptotic cost per recovery pass.
Gaussian elimination finds a nonzero vector when one exists in the span of the three gradients intersected with the $n$ form kernels, in polynomial time by these dimensions and $N\le D$.
The lifting demand gives polynomial further time per selected expression.
Packing a successful output is polynomial time by its coefficient formula with $\ell d_R\le D+d_R$.
Adding these costs for at most two selected expressions and six recovery passes per expression gives $t+O(Q+d_R Q_H+\mu)+\mathsf{poly}(D,\log q)$ including the original description and advice.

add.statement: For prime $q$ with $2\beta<q$ and $24\beta^4<q^3$, the lifting routine $\mathsf{LIFT}$ implemented by the bounded-prefix algorithm below deterministically returns a short multiple of any nonzero $v\in\mathbb F_q^{N+1}$ with $v_0=0$ when one exists, and returns $\bot$ otherwise, in time polynomial in $N,\log q$. After normalization, the prefix lattice on $i$ coordinates is the set of integer vectors reducing to the line spanned by the first $i$ normalized coordinates; bounded means infinity norm at most $\beta$.
add.proof:
For $\beta<1$ return $\bot$, since the box has no nonzero integer vector.
Delete coordinate zero and normalize a nonzero coordinate of $v$ to $v_1=1$ by reordering and scaling.
Four bounded vectors of a prefix lattice have all four-row minors divisible by $q^3$ by Smith form, since their reductions have rank at most one.
The determinant bound $24\beta^4<q^3$ makes each of these minors zero.
Consequently the bounded vectors in each prefix span a rational space of dimension at most three.
Store a bounded basis for this span, starting with $(1)$ in the first coordinate.
At extension $i+1$, every bounded vector lies over the stored prefix span by restriction.
Fraction-free elimination on the stored bounded vectors computes independent polynomial-bit integer equations for that prefix span.
The rows $x_j-v_jx_1=q t_j$ for $2\le j\le i+1$ on candidate extension $x$ are independent modulo the prefix rows by their fresh $t_j$ columns, using integer representatives for $v_j$.
